about: Vectors for the card entry point of @integraledger/lcp: Visa TAP, Mastercard Agent Pay, Visa Intelligent Commerce, Mastercard Verifiable Intent and the plain card checkout. H is SHA-256("abc") from FIPS 180-2 and E is SHA-256 of the empty string. The TAP and Agent Pay signatures are RFC 9421 Ed25519 under RFC 9421's test-key-ed25519, and their nonces the base64 of H or E followed by C2.random. C2 to C9 and T2 to V10 were computed with Node's node:crypto from the profiles, importing no lcp code. The VI strings of `vi` are built from a recipe (compact JSON, members in the order written) with fixed ES256 signatures, which verify under USER (L2i, L2a) and AGENT (L3b); every digest was checked with Python 3.12.3 hashlib.

buyer.about: The buyer gate's rows for this file's pairings, in the form of buyer.json's rows. B2 is the plant: the document advertises H, the hash of the ATR in B6's first check, and the link serves the planted ATR, that ATR with one byte changed; the gate declines hash-mismatch and never calls the signer. B6 is the pairing's bound check over the payment this file already holds: check(ATR, presented) gives H, and check(planted ATR, presented) declines signed-not-bound. Where the ATR is abc, H is its SHA-256 (FIPS 180-2 B.1) and the planted ATR is abd. SHA-256 values are GNU coreutils sha256sum, which openssl dgst -sha256 matches. Bytes are hex. A B2 input names the account, the buyer's inputs and the time (now, in seconds) its build needs. noSignedPayment names each pairing of the file that has no B6 row, and why.

C9.about: TAP requests with two agent-payer-auth signatures. A verifier determines which signature to process by its own policy and configuration (RFC 9421 §3.2, step 1.1), so bound takes the hash only when every agent-payer-auth signature carries it, and the same one. Built as C2's request is.

T2.about: The checkout path, for an agent whose nonce does not carry H: Visa's reference agent's Signature-Input as tap-agent/agent_app.py:1364 writes it (keyId, "; " separators, a UUID nonce), signed as :1331-1338 builds the base, under RFC 9421's test-key-ed25519 in place of Visa's key. Where the signature covers a path ending in a hash, the path carries H and the nonce is not read: a stock agent's 64 random nonce bytes, in the shape of the specification's example nonce, are not read as a hash there (the first T2 row naming a stock agent's nonce; built by node:crypto from the profile, fam-card2's tap-path-rows.mjs).

T3.about: TAP's published requests, as refusal vectors. Multi-line displays are joined with one space, the markdown emphasis and the escape before _ removed. V1 to V3: the TAP specification (https://developer.visa.com/docs/trusted-agent-protocol/trusted-agent-protocol-specifications.md, read 2026-11-16, SHA-256 7f2408c64c2723c4...), lines given; R1 to R3: visa/trusted-agent-protocol at 16d59bd. None carries a hash a merchant issued: V3's nonce is 64 bytes, read as a hash no merchant issued.

V10.about: Verifiable Intent views (spec/credential-format.md §5.4 at agent-intent/verifiable-intent@356c296): an Autonomous chain shaped as the reference SDK example builds it (examples/autonomous_flow.py, examples/helpers.py), with an L2 holding the open checkout and payment mandates, the merchant once for each and two acceptable items as disclosures, under the P-256 keys ISSUER, USER and AGENT. merchantView is §5.4's L2_base_jwt~checkout~item~, the presentation L3b's sd_hash covers; roleView is the SDK example's build_role_presentations view (helpers.py:233-273), the checkout mandate with every acceptable item; fullL2 is the whole Autonomous L2. Built with Node's node:crypto from the profile, not by lcp.
